input.brief: InsightOps: Azure DevOps visibility for sprints, builds, PRs, releases with optional AI; encrypted read-only PATs

direction.name: The quiet instrument
direction.idea: Radical understatement. Where every competitor shouts, this page almost whispers: a headline barely larger than body text, a narrow column, small exact demonstrations, and a great deal of untouched space. The restraint is the claim. It says the thing is simple, finished and sure of itself. This only works when it is carried through completely; one loud element breaks it. In the study, a tool for simple lists sold itself with a 27px headline and 12–14px copy and was one of the most confident pages in the set.
direction.composition: A single column 440–560px wide, placed left of centre (starting at about 22% of the viewport width) or dead centre, running the whole page. The headline is the one large thing on the first screen: two lines at display size (5–7vw), medium weight, starting on the column's left edge and allowed to run wider than the column. The supporting paragraph follows at body size (17–19px) in the full ink. One small primary button and one text link. Below, each point is a short paragraph followed by a compact demonstration or image no wider than the column. Sections are separated only by space (96–140px). Nothing spans the full width until the footer, which is a single quiet line. The first screen is mostly empty and that emptiness is composed: the column's top edge sits at about 30% of the viewport height.
direction.typography: One family, two weights. A display size for the headline (5–7vw), one heading size for section titles (about 32–40px), body at 17–19px, a small size for captions (14–15px). Leading 1.5 for text. Letter-spacing near zero. The typeface must be handsome at small sizes.
direction.colour: Paper and two inks (full and soft). One accent used on exactly one element per screen.
direction.imagery: Precise rather than loud: cropped interface details at true size, and real photographs of the customer's world held to the column width, each doing one job. One short looping clip can sit at column width too. Never a large stock hero image.
direction.richness: Precision. With so little on the page, alignment, spacing and the exact size relationships are the design. Every element shares the column's left edge.
direction.pitfalls: This is the one direction where a small headline is right; the inspector will not object, but do not mix it with a large display line. Emptiness must look decided: keep the column edges exact and the vertical rhythm even. Not suitable when the subject needs emotion or photography to sell. Quiet is not thin: the column must still deliver every piece of content the brief asks for, in full, at 16px or more in the full ink. In blind tests the quiet version lost every time it was quiet everywhere: a small headline beside an empty panel read as unfinished. Quiet means few things, not small things: the headline and the demonstration are large, and every screen holds content.

hero.name: Control that reads the page
hero.blueprint: A near-black or deep neutral ground split into two halves by tone alone: the right half is one step lighter than the left, and they meet at a clean vertical edge at 50%. Left half: a small logo mark top-left at a 40px margin, then two-thirds of empty ground, then everything else anchored bottom-left, 40px from the edges: a one-line headline at clamp(26px, 2.1vw, 32px) in medium weight, one supporting sentence at 17px in the softer ink held to 44ch, and the single action as a light rectangular button. Right half: one fragment of the product, centred, about 450px square, built in HTML and working. It is the product's defining control (a loupe, a picker, a dial, a field) and it acts on the page itself: it reads the real background colour, the real headline size or the pointer position and prints that value in its own readout at 13px. Mark its root with data-ui so the product's own radii and borders apply inside it. There is no navigation bar; one text link sits top-right at 15px.
hero.mobile: The halves stack as two tones. The fragment comes first: 78vw square, centred in the lighter block, which is 58svh tall, still live and reading the page under the visitor's finger. The darker block below holds the headline at 6.4vw on up to two lines, the sentence at 16px and the button, left-aligned at 20px. The logo mark sits top-left over the first block.
hero.headline: One plain line at 26–32px naming what the tool is, up to about 32 characters, wrapping to two lines on a phone.

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: One-size name columns
sections.blueprint: Pure text at one size. Three columns start on columns 1, 4 and 7 of the 12-column grid, leaving columns 10–12 empty on purpose. Each column opens with a group name in full ink and continues with a tight stack of six to ten capability names in the soft ink, all at 16–17px, regular weight, line-height 1.25, no bullets and no symbols; one blank line separates group name from stack. Hovering a name brings it to full ink and shows a one-line description in a fixed spot: the top of the empty columns 10–12, at the same size. The heading is no larger than 28px; two or three words, alone on column 1, 96px above the columns. Give the section 20vh of empty ground above and below, so the smallness reads as decided. Works on light or deep grounds.
sections.mobile: Columns stack with 40px between groups; text rises to 18px with line-height 1.4 for touch. Group names stay in full ink. Hover descriptions are dropped; each group ends instead with one sentence in the soft ink that sums it up. The heading is 24px, 48px above.

sections.name: Call and response column
sections.blueprint: The sequence is shown as what you give and what comes back, in one narrow column 560px wide starting at column 4, or on the page's text axis. Three exchanges, 88px apart. Each opens with a sentence at 20px medium that begins with its order word ('First, install it.' 'Then ask for a chart.'). 16px under it, the call: the literal thing the user enters, in a filled panel one tone off the ground, radius 8px, padding 20px. For a developer tool that is real code in `<pre><code>` at 14px with a working copy button; otherwise it is the product's own input holding real typed text. Under the call, indented 56px, the response: a true-size fragment marked data-ui showing what the product returns. The third response is the finished result and breaks out of the column, 760px wide, running to column 12. The heading, two to four words at 28px, sits 56px above the first sentence.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Calls and responses stack without the indent; a 24px gap and a lighter panel tone set the response apart. Code panels scroll sideways inside themselves. The final result runs edge to edge at true size, cropped on the right if wider.

sections.name: Recognition as a table
sections.blueprint: Awards, press mentions or credits set as a four-column table with no lines. The heading is two or three words at about 5vw, stepped over two lines with the second line indented by two columns, and occupies columns 1–7. The table begins 72px below and spans columns 1–12 on a fixed grid: year in columns 1–2, project or title in 3–6, awarding body or publication in 7–10, the award itself in 11–12, right-aligned. Rows are set at 16–17px with 14px of padding above and below; every second row carries a background tone one step from the ground, running the full table width, which replaces rules. Year groups are separated by one blank row, and the year is printed only on the first row of its group. Use a real `<table>` with `border-collapse: collapse` and no borders.
sections.mobile: The heading drops to 11vw. Each table row becomes a two-line block: title on the first line in the full ink, then body and award on the second in the softer ink. The year stands once as a 22px figure above its group. Alternate blocks keep the background tone.

sections.name: A single quiet line
sections.blueprint: No footer block at all. After at least 30svh of empty page ground, one baseline 30px above the bottom edge carries three items in the page's ordinary small text size (14–16px), the same size and weight as the navigation: at the left margin, what this is in three or four words; centred, two to five links separated by 24px of space; at the right margin, the year and a privacy link. Use a three-column grid (1fr auto 1fr) so the centre group is truly centred whatever the side lengths. No logo, no background change, no line above it, no columns. Links are in the full ink; the rest in the softer ink. If the page has a narrow text column, the three items may instead sit on that column's left edge as one wrapped line. The restraint only works if the page above has already made its invitation.
sections.mobile: Three short lines at 14px on the left margin with 8px between them: the description, the links on one wrapped line, then year and privacy. Links stay in the full ink. Leave 20svh of empty ground above and 24px below.

references.name: Gil Huybrecht
references.idea: A portfolio as a contact sheet: every project is a numbered run of miniature page screenshots on black, and all text is set at one small size.
references.hero: Black field on a seven-column grid with 14px margins. The top band is plain white text at one size, about 16px: name in column one, availability in column two, a services list from column three, a longer awards list from column five, then 'Profile' and 'Email me' at the right. List items are indented one step under their label. Below the lists roughly 300px of black is left empty. At mid-height the thumbnail grid begins: one small website screenshot per column, about 190px wide, each topped by a number at its right corner, with the project name over the first of each run. Two tiny toggle chips sit in the bottom corners.
references.type: One neo-grotesk at a single size, about 16px (1.1vw), medium-bold with tight tracking, white on black, for everything: name, lists, labels, numbers, footer. There is no headline; hierarchy comes only from column position and indentation.
references.colour: #000000 #fcfcfc #272727 #8a8a8a — Pure black with white text; the only colour is whatever appears inside the screenshot thumbnails. Inactive toggle words drop to mid-grey on a dark grey chip.
references.imagery: Miniature full-page captures of the designer's client sites, uncropped at natural aspect ratios, square corners, no frames or shadows, about 190px wide, sitting directly on black.
references.layout: Seven equal columns with 14px gutters and margins for the whole page. Thumbnails align to columns but not to rows: each hangs from its own label at its own height, so bottoms are ragged. Projects flow continuously and wrap across rows.

sections.description: A seven-column field of screenshot thumbnails on black. Each project is a consecutive run of four to six thumbnails; the project name sits above the first, and every thumbnail carries its sequence number right-aligned above it in the same 16px white. Thumbnails keep their real proportions, so a row mixes 100px-tall and 280px-tall items with ragged bottoms and about 90px of black between rows. Runs break mid-row and continue on the next line with no divider.

View toggles. Two fixed chip pairs sit in the viewport's bottom corners: the left switches between a grid and a gallery view, the right between a normal and a novelty perspective mode. Each pair is a small dark-grey rounded rectangle containing two words, the active one white and the inactive grey, at the same 16px as all other text.

After about a screen of empty black, one band of text on the same seven columns: year and privacy link stacked at the left, then two columns of stacked social links, then two single links toward the right edge. Same size and weight as the header, no rule, no logo.

steal: Set every piece of text on the page at one size and weight and build hierarchy only from column position and a one-step indent under labels.
Show projects as numbered runs of uncropped page screenshots at natural heights on a strict column grid, leaving the bottoms ragged.
Leave a deliberate 300px void between the text header and the first row of work so the lists read as a letterhead.
references.media: A contact-sheet wall: one fixed WebGL canvas draws about 84 full-page screenshots of client sites at a single 190px width and their native ratios, every page of each project in reading order. Once scrolled, every screen is about three rows, roughly 48% picture and 52% black, with text under 1% and the labels above each frame, never on it; there is no video.
references.motion: The preloader counts at about 13% a second for some 7-8s while the screenshot textures load, although the document loaded in 1.66s; then the first-row thumbnails rise into their slots in random order and a dark veil lifts. Lenis over a 4440px scroll proxy redraws the fixed wall with no pins or reveals; panel and hover moves use transform .75s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1), and pictures fade over 1s ease-out on the phone.

references.name: Cursor Compile
references.idea: The event name drawn as seven looping one-line curves in seven colours, more signature than logotype, on an otherwise whisper-quiet off-white page whose images are re-rendered as rows of coloured characters.
references.hero: Warm off-white field with no header or navigation. Starting about 23% down, a line-drawn wordmark spans from 8% to 92% of the width and about 29% of the height: each letter is a single 2px stroke looping like a Lissajous figure, each in a different colour (orange, green, olive, lilac, black, brown, blue), overlapping its neighbours. Directly beneath, two 14px captions, one flush left in ink and one flush right in grey. After a gap of about 20% of the viewport, three equal columns sit at the bottom, each topped by a hairline: an 18px statement, a grey 14px paragraph, and an email field over a full-width near-black rectangular button.
references.type: The only large lettering is the drawn wordmark. All real text is CursorGothic regular in two sizes, 18px and 14px (the largest text on the page is 1.8vw), sentence case, with hierarchy made by ink versus mid-grey rather than by size or weight.
references.colour: #edece8 #26251e #f07a1f #2e9e3a #2f6bf0 #9b8ff0 — Warm paper ground with near-black and grey text. The wordmark's colours return one at a time as the single ink of each character-rendered image (lilac, teal, green, orange). Event photos are dark and warm.
references.imagery: Two kinds: landmarks and speaker portraits redrawn as rows of tiny characters in one saturated colour on a tint of the same colour; and dark, warm documentary event photos. All are square-cornered rectangles in strict rows.
references.layout: About 7% side margins on a three-column grid. Each section has a small two-line heading at left (title in ink, subtitle in grey), then a row or carousel of equal tiles with one-line captions beneath. Very large vertical gaps between sections; a denser photo grid near the end.

sections.description: Tour dates as a three-column grid of 3:2 tiles. Each tile is a city landmark rendered entirely in rows of small characters in one colour on a pale tint of that colour: lilac, teal, green, orange. Under each tile, one caption line: city name in ink, date in grey straight after it, and a status word flush right. A fourth tile wraps alone to the left of a second row, leaving two columns empty.

Session recordings as stacked carousels. A small heading and grey subtitle, then per stage a tiny label at left with two arrow glyphs at far right and a row of 16:9 dark photo tiles, two full tiles visible and a third cropped by the margin. Each tile has a small white event tag in its bottom-left corner. Caption beneath: speaker name in ink followed by the talk title in grey on the same line.

Speaker row: one-line heading at left, arrows at right, then four near-square portrait tiles with 8px gaps, each a face drawn in horizontal rows of characters in one colour on its tint (orange, green, lilac, teal). Some tiles show only plain stripes with the face barely emerging, so portraits appear to resolve from lines as they load or on hover.

After a three-column photo grid with mixed landscape and portrait crops and 8px gaps, the page ends on an empty off-white screen holding one centred sentence at 18px and a small dark pill button beneath it. There are no footer columns, links or legal rows.

steal: Draw the name as one continuous thin looping stroke per letter, each in a different colour, and let it be the only large element on the page.
Keep all text at two small sizes and build hierarchy from ink versus grey on the same line (name in ink, detail in grey right after it).
Re-render photographs as rows of tiny characters in a single saturated colour on a tint of that colour, one colour per tile.

references.name: Typewave
references.idea: A plugin about type scales sold on a near-black page where flat saturated fields (orange, lime, blue) act as stages for the plugin's own dark interface.
references.hero: Near-black field. Nav row at the top: pixel-block logo and wordmark left, four plain links centred (one carrying a tiny lime tag), a cream rectangular button with a Figma glyph right. The headline sits centred around mid-height: three lines at about 6.7vw, medium weight, off-white, with the third line recoloured pale lime. Below it a three-line 18px paragraph held to about 45% of the width, then a small cream button repeating the nav action. About 150px lower, the top edge of a flat orange slab, 70% of the viewport wide with barely rounded corners, peeks over the fold; it holds the plugin window.
references.type: Roobert throughout: weight 500 for the 96px headline with slight negative tracking, 16-18px body, 28px card headings, about four sizes in all. Sentence case everywhere; the only emphasis device is recolouring one headline line.
references.colour: #0f0f0e #191918 #e6e3da #f88616 #e4f283 #1463ff — Warm near-black ground with cream text. Orange, lime and electric blue never colour paragraphs; they only fill the rectangles behind product screenshots and the matching step-number chips.
references.imagery: Dark plugin windows with a soft drop shadow, floated centred on flat saturated rectangles (orange, lime, blue, one pink); the rectangles are near square-cornered and inset inside a slightly lighter dark card.
references.layout: Centred hero, then a 1000px container of full-width dark cards, each split one-third text and two-thirds colour stage. Export features alternate text and tile left to right. A small two-button bar stays pinned bottom-centre.

sections.description: Three stacked cards in a slightly lighter black, each about 1000 by 350px. Left third: a 16px square number chip in the card's accent colour at the top, a three-line 28px heading under it, and a grey 12px paragraph pushed to the card's bottom edge, leaving a tall gap between. Right two-thirds: a flat colour rectangle inset 16px with the dark plugin window centred and shadowed on it. Cards differ only by hue: lime, orange, blue.

Between demo blocks a single left-aligned sentence at about 36px sits alone on black with some 300px of space above and below. Its words light up from dark grey to cream one after another as you scroll, so mid-capture the sentence trails off into the background. The pinned two-button bar is the only other element on screen.

Export options as alternating rows. One side: a square colour tile (lime, then orange) holding a code-panel screenshot. Other side: a 24px heading, a five-line grey paragraph and a row of three or four small monochrome tool logos. Tile and text swap sides on each row, and the tiles are staggered vertically so one row's tile overlaps the next row's text band.

steal: Stage dark UI screenshots on flat saturated rectangles instead of on the page background, so the colour does the branding and the UI stays legible.
Pin the paragraph to the bottom of a tall card and the heading to the top so the gap between them becomes the card's composition.
Colour-key each step: the number chip and the stage behind the screenshot share one hue and nothing else on the card uses it.
